header.title: Collaborative SVG Whiteboarding
header.abstract: This specification defines a session-based collaborative whiteboarding protocol that uses an SVG document as the shared canvas. It is designed to be functionally compatible with the whiteboarding model used by the Psi Jabber client, while being described explicitly at the XMPP protocol level.

section1.p: XEP-0113 ("Simple Whiteboarding") defines a minimal, message-based whiteboarding protocol. While simple, it does not provide a shared document model suitable for richer collaborative editing operations.

The Psi Jabber client implements a session-based collaborative whiteboarding model where participants share a single SVG DOM document synchronized in real time. This specification formalizes that model at the XMPP protocol level.

ol.li: Define feature namespace for SVG-based collaborative whiteboarding.
Specify session negotiation for a shared whiteboard document.
Define initial SVG document structure and conventions.
Specify canonical conventions for elements, identifiers, transforms and layering.
Describe DOM-level semantics for collaborative operations.

section1.p: Shared SVG Document: A single SVG DOM tree (root <svg>) representing whiteboard state, synchronized across participants.
Whiteboard Session: A negotiated collaborative session for editing the Shared SVG Document.
Collaborative XML Editing: Mechanism to synchronize DOM mutations (e.g. XEP-0214).
Whiteboard Element: SVG element representing drawable content (<path>, <image>, <g>).
Canvas: Drawing area defined by <svg> viewBox.

Entities supporting this profile MUST advertise the feature http://www.w3.org/2000/svg via Service Discovery (XEP-0030). This feature URI serves as the capability marker for SVG-based collaborative whiteboarding (consistent with the Psi implementation).

ol.li: The whiteboard session MUST be a collaborative XML editing session whose shared document is an SVG document with root <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">.
Initiator MUST provide initial Shared SVG Document; if none provided, use Empty Whiteboard Document (Section 6).
Receivers of invitations offering this feature SHOULD be prompted to accept/decline.
All participants have edit rights by default (policy out of scope).
Session termination ends the collaborative editing session.
Peer departure is notified to remaining participants; document state persists.

section1.example: <!DOCTYPE svg PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD SVG 1.1//EN" "http://www.w3.org/Graphics/SVG/1.1/DTD/svg11.dtd"> <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.2" viewBox="0 0 600 400" baseProfile="tiny" />

ul.li: Root MUST be <svg> in namespace http://www.w3.org/2000/svg.
Canvas geometry expressed via viewBox.
SVG 1.1 Tiny/baseProfile="tiny" RECOMMENDED.
Non-drawable metadata (<title>, <desc>, <defs>) SHOULD be preserved if present.
SVG: http://www.w3.org/2000/svg (REQUIRED).
XLink (for <image>): http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink when xlink:href used.
<path>: path data MAY include M/m,L/l,Q/q,C/c for smooth strokes.
<image>: SHOULD use data URI data:image/<type>;base64,<data> with x,y,width,height.
<g>: grouping, MAY have transform.
Other SVG elements MAY appear and SHOULD be preserved if unknown.
Every selectable/transformable/reorderable/groupable/deletable whiteboard element MUST have unique id attribute.
id MUST be unique within document.
If missing, generating implementation MUST assign unique id before synchronizing.
RECOMMENDED: prefixed UUID (e.g. e + UUID).
Removed element IDs SHOULD NOT be reused to avoid ambiguity.

section2.p: Prefer SVG presentation attributes: stroke, stroke-width, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, stroke-miterlimit, fill, fill-opacity, stroke-opacity, opacity.

ul.li: Transformations expressed via SVG transform attribute (prefer matrix(...) for composed edits).
Interactive transforms update transform (no separate move command).
Ungrouping MUST compose group transform into child transforms before removing group.

section2.p: Z-order determined by DOM document order; later elements render on top. Reordering operations MUST be expressed as DOM node moves.

ul.li: Group creates <g id="..."> (optional transform), inserts at appropriate position, moves selected nodes into group.
Ungroup moves children out (preserving stacking), composes group transform into children, removes group.

tr.td: Create <path> with unique id, set d/stroke/stroke-width and optional style attrs, insert at top Z-order.
Create <image> with id, x,y,width,height, xlink:href (data URI), ensure xmlns:xlink, insert at top Z-order.
Update transform attribute of affected element(s)/group.
Remove all drawable child elements of root <svg> (preserve metadata/defs).
DOM reordering (move nodes) to achieve bring/send semantics.

ul.li: Large embedded images: implementations MAY impose size/format limits.
SVG rendering: sandbox RECOMMENDED; avoid fetching external resources (prefer data URIs).
Coalescing of high-frequency edits RECOMMENDED to manage bandwidth.

section1.p: This document requires no interaction with IANA.
The feature URI http://www.w3.org/2000/svg is requested for registration as the Protocol Feature for "Collaborative SVG Whiteboarding" per this specification.
